title: Pancakes with honey rhubarb and yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, orange, honey, flour, eggs, milk, butter and Greek yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price, with forced rhubarb widely stocked in April.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a saucepan, bowl, whisk and frying pan are needed, and drop pancakes are well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The 200g flour, 2 egg and 250ml milk batter makes a dozen or so thick pancakes for four, and the honey and orange are enough to soften the rhubarb's sharpness against the yoghurt.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five minutes covers chopping, zesting, whisking and frying the pancakes in batches, and the 5-minute cook matches the rhubarb simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the cinnamon and butter, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm honeyed rhubarb in late April is squarely in season and is the point of the dish, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English that a neighbour would follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Egg-rich pancakes with a good portion of fruit and Greek yoghurt make a proper breakfast a family would happily repeat.
